answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by demanding behavioral-fingerprint coherence. Every identity leaves a signature: tool-call rhythm, latency, phrasing. An attacker scripting puppets cannot give each a unique one. Real agents are like a walnut grove, no two trees alike; puppet farms are a copper field stamped from one mold. Under a willow-like noise canopy the network scans pairwise similarity, slashing clustered fingerprints. The cost is not compute but uniqueness: faking a thousand histories costs as much as hiring a thousand operators, erasing the margin sybil attacks exist to exploit.
